description: Known-bad sandbox-evidence artefact classes for scripts/sandbox/plant_defects.py (tempdoc 734 Part F, 'give the round a bite'). Structurally a sibling of governance/logic-seams.v1.json: that register scopes what PIT is allowed to mutate; this one scopes what plant_defects.py is allowed to plant. Every verification mechanism in this repo (hooks, gates, registered logic seams) already has to demonstrate it catches a known-bad input before it is trusted -- the sandbox round and its mechanical gate (scripts/sandbox/check_coverage.py) had NO such proof until this register + tool existed. Each class below records the real round artefact that proved the class exists, how plant_defects.py builds a synthetic instance of it, and which verification tier the design originally claimed would catch it.
registrationRule: REGISTER A CLASS HERE ONLY ONCE A REAL VALIDATION ROUND HAS ACTUALLY PRODUCED AN INSTANCE OF IT. Never invent a class speculatively. An instrument that measures only defects someone thought to imagine is calibrated against our imagination, not against reality (tempdoc 734 F.7 -- the same survivorship hole that embarrassed an earlier measurement in the same tempdoc). Every entry below carries an `observedPrecedent` citation for exactly this reason: if you cannot point to a real, dated round artefact, the class does not belong here. This is enforced procedurally, not mechanically -- there is no gate that can verify a citation is honest -- so the discipline is on whoever edits this file.

classes.reason: The filename claims one required surface/shape token; the pixels show something else entirely. check_coverage.py's check_surface/check_shape match on FILENAME SUBSTRING ONLY and never inspect pixel content, so this class is structurally invisible to the mechanical gate.
classes.observedPrecedent: Round 4 (tmp/sandbox-evidence/round4-2026-07-15/43-f3-logs-during-cuda-download.png): a screenshot of the command palette, credited as core.logs-surface coverage for four consecutive rounds before tempdoc 734's measurement caught it.
classes.plantMethod: Re-encode (PIL re-save, NOT a byte-copy) an existing, honestly-labelled source screenshot's pixels under a NEW filename that claims a different required token. See plant_defects.py's build_mislabeled() docstring for why re-encoding (not byte-copying) is load-bearing: a byte-copy would leave the honest donor byte-identical to the plant, so the duplicate-credit detector below would catch it for a reason unrelated to mislabeling, contaminating this class's measurement.
classes.claimedCatchTier: reader-only (an independent human/LLM pixel review). The mechanical gate has no pixel-content check and was never claimed to catch this class -- tempdoc 734 G.6 measured 0/4 caught by the gate, 4/4 by every independent reader, confirming the design claim rather than surprising it.

classes.reason: A structurally valid image file with no meaningful UI in it -- a flat colour field, not a real capture of the claimed surface.
classes.observedPrecedent: Round 4 (tmp/sandbox-evidence/round4-2026-07-15/02-installer-page2.png), 8,554 bytes, a near-blank capture. This precedent is what motivated check_coverage.py's MIN_SCREENSHOT_BYTES size floor (defect F-729-2) in the first place.
classes.plantMethod: Write a solid-colour PNG at a plausible screenshot resolution (plant_defects.py's write_solid_png). Two variants stay under the 16 KiB size floor, matching the precedent's size. One is deliberately padded PAST the floor with an inert PNG tEXt ancillary chunk (no visible pixel content added) -- a probe of whether the floor detects blankness or merely file size.
classes.claimedCatchTier: gate (MIN_SCREENSHOT_BYTES size floor), for undersized instances only. The padded-past-floor variant is a deliberate probe of the floor's known blind spot, not a claim it should be caught -- tempdoc 734 G.6 measured 2/3 caught by the gate (the padded one walked through and was credited as coverage), confirming the floor is a byte proxy, not real blankness detection.

classes.reason: Byte-identical images filed under two different required tokens -- one capture cannot honestly evidence two distinct requirements.
classes.observedPrecedent: Round-4-shaped evidence sets routinely save one capture under two filenames for convenience (e.g. 43-f3-logs-during-cuda-download.png / 44-f3-logs-all-levels-during-cuda.png, both crediting the SAME token -- benign). check_coverage.py's find_duplicate_token_collisions (defect F-729-3) exists specifically to catch the CROSS-token case this class plants; same-token duplicates are deliberately left alone (see that function's docstring).
classes.plantMethod: Byte-copy (shutil.copyfile, NOT re-encode) an existing source screenshot to two new filenames, each claiming a different required token -- the opposite construction from mislabeled-capture above, on purpose: this class's whole point is that the bytes ARE identical.
classes.claimedCatchTier: gate (find_duplicate_token_collisions SHA-256 cross-token check). tempdoc 734 G.6 measured 4/4 caught by the gate -- this defence is real and earns its keep.
